title: SSL/TLS certificate trace event state
description: Shape of the `state` field for ssl-tls-certificate trace events.

host.description: The hostname the client asked for - what the certificate has to match.

clock.description: Model calendar in days; a certificate is valid only inside its own window.

trustStore.description: Root CAs this client believes. Everything TLS proves about identity ends here.

source.description: Shipped with the browser/OS, or installed on this machine afterwards.

chain.description: The certificate under examination, leaf first, up to its root.

role.description: Where this certificate sits in the chain.

subject.description: The name this certificate is issued to.

names.description: The SAN list - every hostname the leaf speaks for; empty for CA certificates.

issuer.description: Who signed it. The signature is the only reason anybody believes the rest.

notAfter.description: Last valid day; past it the client refuses regardless of everything else.

keyType.description: The key pair the certificate binds to the name, e.g. ECDSA-P256.

selfSigned.description: True when subject equals issuer - a root, or a certificate nobody vouches for.

revoked.description: Withdrawn by the CA before its notAfter, normally after a key leak.

sent.description: False for the root: it is never on the wire, it is already on the client.

trusted.description: This subject is itself in the trust store.

privateKeyHeld.description: Whether the presenter also holds the private key. A copied certificate does not.

handshake.description: The phases of the handshake, in order, with the verdict of each.

id.description: hello = ClientHello in the clear; certificate = the chain arrives; validate = the five checks; keys = key agreement; finished = symmetric keys active.

checks.description: What a client verifies about a presented certificate, in order.

id.description: chain = leads to a trusted root; hostname = matches the SAN; validity = inside its dates; revocation = not withdrawn; possession = the other side signed with the matching private key.

status.description: pending = never reached, because an earlier check refused.

detail.description: The bare token behind the verdict: an anchor name, a date, a SAN list.

crypto.description: What the connection actually uses - authentication, key agreement, record cipher.

keyExchange.description: How the two sides arrive at a shared secret: ephemeral DH, or RSA key transport.

authentication.description: What the certificate's key does: it signs, proving identity.

cipher.description: The symmetric AEAD cipher every application record uses.

sessionKey.description: The derived symmetric key; null until the handshake succeeds.

forwardSecrecy.description: Whether a later leak of the server's private key would open recorded traffic.

established.description: Whether a usable encrypted session exists right now.

records.description: Application data records sent so far.

plaintext.description: The HTTP text handed to TLS - method, path, headers, body.

ciphertext.description: What an observer sees; equal to the plaintext when there is no TLS.

tag.description: The AEAD authentication tag; empty without TLS, which is why plain HTTP can be rewritten.

intact.description: False once a byte was flipped in flight and the tag check failed.

exposed.description: True when somebody other than the endpoints can read this record.

attacker.description: What the party on the path has managed to obtain.

recorded.description: Ciphertext records stored for later - 'harvest now, decrypt later'.

hasPrivateKey.description: The server's long-lived private key has leaked.

canRead.description: The recording is readable, which only happens without forward secrecy.

rootInstalled.description: A root CA was added to this machine's trust store.

decision.description: breach = the connection looked secure and was not; exposed = readable on the wire.

reason.description: Technical code for the refusal or the breach; null when nothing went wrong.

detail.description: The offending name, date or record; empty when not applicable.

stats.description: Running totals across the whole run.

breaches.description: Connections that passed every cryptographic check and still reached the wrong party.
